info.title: Call2Me API
info.description:
# Call2Me Voice AI Platform API

Programmatic interface to build, deploy and operate voice AI agents that can place
and receive phone calls in real time. Designed to be consumed by humans **and** by
AI agent frameworks (function-calling LLMs, MCP servers, automation platforms like
Composio, Pipedream, Zapier, n8n).

## What you can do

- **Place outbound calls** — give an agent a phone number to dial; the AI handles
  the conversation end-to-end and returns a transcript + recording.
- **Manage AI agents** — create personalities, attach voices, system prompts,
  knowledge bases and post-call actions.
- **Run bulk campaigns** — upload a CSV of contacts, set retry rules, monitor
  per-contact outcome.
- **Schedule calls** — one-shot or recurring (cron-like) outbound calls.
- **Knowledge base (RAG)** — upload documents/URLs so the agent answers from your
  data with reduced hallucination.
- **Inbound** — provision phone numbers that route to your agents.

## Common LLM tool-calling use cases

| Goal | Endpoint |
|------|----------|
| "Call this person and read them this script" | `POST /v1/calls` |
| "Schedule a follow-up tomorrow at 14:00" | `POST /v1/schedules` |
| "Bulk-call these 200 leads" | `POST /v1/campaigns` + `/upload-csv` |
| "Get the transcript of last call" | `GET /v1/calls/{id}` |
| "Add this PDF to the agent's brain" | `POST /v1/knowledge-base/{id}/sources` |

## Authentication

Every request requires a Bearer token issued from the dashboard:

```
Authorization: Bearer c2m_sk_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Get your API key from the [API Keys page](https://dash.call2me.app/api-keys).
Keys are scoped per-workspace and can be rotated/revoked any time.

## Rate Limits

| Plan | Requests/min | Concurrent Calls |
|------|-------------|------------------|
| Free | 60 | 1 |
| Pro | 600 | 10 |
| Enterprise | Unlimited | Unlimited |

## SDKs & Integrations

- [Python SDK](https://github.com/call2me/python-sdk)
- [Node.js SDK](https://github.com/call2me/node-sdk)
- OpenAPI 3.1 spec: `/openapi.json` (use it to generate clients or register the
  service with AI tool platforms)

## Support

- Email: support@call2me.app
- Docs: https://docs.call2me.app
- Discord: https://discord.gg/call2me

post.description:
Create a new voice AI agent. Required: `agent_name`, `response_engine` (which LLM and how to invoke it), and a `voice_id` from `/v1/voices`. Optional: `system_prompt`, `first_message`, `language`, `interruption_sensitivity`, `knowledge_base_ids` and `function_definitions`.

Agent creation no longer requires email verification.

get.description: Returns all agents owned by this workspace, newest first. Use `limit` and `offset` for pagination. With an ephemeral end-user token (agents:read scope), returns trimmed public cards only (agent_id, name, language, voice_id, public_metadata) — hidden agents excluded, ordered by public_metadata.order.

200.description: Agents in this workspace, newest first (trimmed public cards for ephemeral tokens).

get.description: Retrieve a single agent's full configuration: prompts, voice, model, language, knowledge base bindings, function definitions, post-call actions and assigned phone numbers. With an ephemeral end-user token, returns only the trimmed public card; hidden agents return 404.

200.description: The full agent configuration (trimmed public card for ephemeral tokens).

patch.description: Partial update — only fields included in the request body are modified; omitted fields keep their current values. Use this to tweak prompts, swap voices, attach/detach knowledge bases or update function definitions without recreating the agent.

delete.description: Permanently delete an agent. This is **irreversible**. Active calls/campaigns/schedules referencing this agent will fail until you point them at a different agent. Phone numbers previously assigned to this agent become unassigned (not deleted).

post.description: Create a new agent that is an exact copy of an existing agent — useful for A/B testing prompts or branching variants. Phone number assignments are **not** copied (assign new numbers to the duplicate via `/v1/phone-numbers`). The duplicate's name will have a `(Copy)` suffix.

201.description: A new agent that is a copy of the source.

Get aggregated statistics across all agents for today.

Returns total calls and cost for the current day.

Get real-time statistics for an agent.

Returns usage metrics like total calls, average duration, tokens used, and costs.

post.description:
Probe a custom-function webhook URL and report what came back.

Same safety rails as the voice-agent runtime path:
  - https only
  - SSRF guard
  - 8s timeout
  - body truncated to 1500 chars

Initiate an outbound phone call. The platform will dial `to_number` from `from_number` (a phone number you own on this workspace), connect the configured AI agent, and begin a real-time voice conversation. The call is placed asynchronously — this endpoint returns immediately with `call_id` and `status='queued'`; poll `GET /v1/calls/{id}` or subscribe to webhooks to track progress.

**Required**: an active agent (`agent_id`) and a phone number assigned to your workspace (`from_number`). If `from_number` is omitted, the agent's assigned phone number is used automatically.

**Cost**: deducted from your wallet per minute of talk time. The request fails with `402` if balance is insufficient.

400.description: No phone number assigned, demo number used for outbound, or other validation error.

get.description: List calls in this workspace, newest first. Supports filtering by `agent_id`, `status` (queued/active/completed/failed/canceled) and `direction` (outbound/inbound). Use `limit` and `offset` for pagination. To retrieve full call details (transcript, recording), call `GET /v1/calls/{id}` for a specific call.

Retrieve a single call by ID. Returns the conversation transcript (speaker-attributed), recording URL (signed for download), call duration, disconnect reason, and any post-call analysis (sentiment, summary, function-call results). Use this endpoint after a call completes to feed transcript/summary back into your downstream workflow (CRM update, ticket creation, follow-up trigger).

200.description: Full call object including transcript, recording URL, status and post-call analysis.

404.description: Call not found in this workspace.

delete.description: Permanently removes the call record (transcript, metadata, analysis) from this workspace. Note: the underlying recording file in object storage is **not** deleted automatically — request a separate recording purge if you need full erasure (e.g. GDPR right-to-be-forgotten requests).

post.description: Forcefully terminate an ongoing call (e.g. when an automation decides the conversation should stop early). The call is marked `disconnection_reason='agent_hangup'`. Calls that are not currently `ongoing` cannot be ended this way.

get.summary: Get a signed URL for the call recording
get.description: Generate a short-lived signed URL (1 hour) for the call's audio recording. Use this to download/stream the recording directly from object storage without exposing long-lived credentials. Suitable for embedding in QA dashboards, sentiment analysis pipelines, or compliance archival.

200.description: A temporary signed URL pointing to the audio recording (valid for 1 hour).

get.summary: Export the call as a vCon container
get.description: Export a completed call in the vCon standard format — a portable, self-contained record of the conversation holding the participants, the turn-by-turn dialog, the recording reference and the post-call analysis (summary, sentiment, custom extractions). Use it to hand conversation data to downstream systems without a proprietary shape. Opt-in per agent: enable `enable_vcon_export` on the agent first.

200.description: The conversation as an IETF vCon JSON container (draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-container): parties, dialog and analysis.

404.description: Call not found, or vCon export is not enabled for its agent.

post.description:
Transfer credit from the reseller's own wallet to one of their members.

A reseller buys credit from us and resells it; this is how they hand a
slice of their balance to a customer. It is a MOVE, not a mint: the same
amount leaves the owner's wallet as arrives in the member's, so no one can
create balance out of nothing.

Every guard here matters, because the request body names the account being
paid:
  * caller must own at least one member (_verify_tenant_owner);
  * the target must be *their* member — checked with tenant_owner_id, so
    naming a stranger's user_id credits nobody;
  * amount is bounded above zero and at 1000 by the schema, so a negative
    value cannot be used to drain a member;
  * both writes run in ONE transaction — a crash between them would
    otherwise duplicate or destroy money;
  * the debit uses the same add_wallet_balance function as every other
    movement, which locks the row and refuses to go below zero.

post.description:
Purchase a phone number from Telnyx, charge user, bind to their account.

Security rules:
  - User must have made at least one paid top-up (not just signup bonus).
    Trial users cannot spend their bonus on number rentals.
  - Balance must cover upfront charge.
  - Only allowed countries (platform_settings.telnyx_allowed_countries).

Create a Paddle checkout session for buying a phone number.

Flow for trial users (no paid top-up yet):
  1. Validate the number is still available on Telnyx.
  2. Create a pending_number_purchases row (soft lock, 30 min TTL).
  3. Open Paddle checkout with custom_data = {intent: 'BUY_NUMBER', pending_id}.
  4. Webhook fires on payment → we order from Telnyx & bind to the user.

Paid users should just use /purchase directly — this endpoint is explicitly
for the first-time/no-balance path.

get.description:

  - User has NOT made a paid topup (paid users buy real numbers)

Note: "has paid" users can still reserve, but they're encouraged to buy.
We don't block them — they can demo if they choose. But UI shows "Buy Number"
as primary for paid users.

post.description:
Reserve a demo number for 15 minutes.

Atomic flow:
  1. Verify eligibility (one-per-lifetime)
  2. Lock a pool row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
  3. Insert demo_reservations row
  4. Mark pool row as 'reserved'
  5. Insert phone_numbers row pointing to user+agent
  6. All inside a transaction — rollback on any failure

get.description:
Interpreted calls for this workspace, live ones first.

Serves the panel's monitoring list: who was rung, who was dialled, whether
the two legs actually connected, and for how long. Interpreter rooms are
identified by `call_type = 'interpreter'` (set at insert time in
`start_interpreted_call`), so this never mixes in ordinary agent calls.

`interpreter_id` narrows the list to one interpreter's own calls (the
per-interpreter detail page); it reads `metadata->>'interpreter_id'`,
which only rows written since that field was added carry.

`offset` + the returned `total` drive the panel's pagination. `total` is
counted under the same filters as the page itself, so the control never
offers a page that would come back empty.

Owner-side kill switch for a live browser call.

The address is shareable and the owner pays for whoever walks in, so
they need a way to end a call they are not part of — a guest who leaves
the tab open, or a conversation that should not be running. Deleting the
LiveKit room is what actually disconnects people; closing our own rows
without it would only hide a call that is still burning balance.

post.description:
Public: admit a visitor and issue their LiveKit token.

This is the enforcement point for every rule in this module — balance,
passcode and capacity — because the token is the only thing that
actually opens the room. A visitor who skips the page and calls this
endpoint directly hits exactly the same checks.

schema.title: Response Join Web Room V1 T  Slug  Join Post

post.description:
Public: release a seat when a visitor closes their tab.

Best-effort — a browser that dies without sending this leaves the seat
held, which is what the stale-session sweep is for. Returning 200 for an
unknown room keeps this safe to call blindly from `beforeunload`.

`failed=true` means the browser never reached the room (the SDK would not
load, or `room.connect` timed out). That attempt is refunded: it would
otherwise burn one of three daily demos without the visitor hearing
anything. See `_refund_public_demo`.

post.description:
Uzantı içinden giriş yapan kullanıcının cihazını hesabına bağlar.

NEDEN AYRI UÇ: `/link/request` + `/link/confirm` postadan geçen yol için
var — kullanıcının parolası yoksa ya da uzantıya parola yazmak
istemiyorsa. Uzantı artık kendi içinde giriş yapabiliyor (e-posta+şifre
ya da Google) ve o durumda posta turuna gerek yok: kimlik zaten JWT ile
kanıtlanmış.

BU UÇ OLMADAN uzantıdan giriş yapan kullanıcının cihazı "kimliksiz"
kalıyordu: çeviri oturumları `device_id` ile açılıyor ve kota o kimlikten
okunuyor, dolayısıyla 60 dakikalık hakkını göremeyip 5 dakikada
takılıyordu.

E-POSTA DOĞRULAMASI ARANMAZ, bilerek: kullanıcı zaten giriş yapabildiyse
hesabı var demektir. `/link/confirm` doğrulamayı postaya tıklayarak
kanıtlıyordu; burada kanıt JWT'nin kendisi.

post.description:
Çıkış yaparken cihazın hesap bağını koparır.

NEDEN GEREKLİ: `/config` kimliksiz bir uçtur (device_id ile çağrılır) ve
bağlı cihazda hesabın E-POSTASINI döndürür — arayüz "kim giriş yapmış"ı
göstersin diye. Uzantıdan çıkış yapmak yalnız token'ı siliyordu, bağ
yerinde kalıyordu; ortak bir makinede çıkış yapan kullanıcının e-posta
adresi bir sonraki kişiye görünüyordu.

CİHAZ KİMLİĞİ SİLİNMEZ, yalnız bağ düşer: kimliği silmek kimliksiz
kotayı sıfırlar ve "çıkış yap → 5 dakika daha" açığı açardı.

Yalnız KENDİ cihazını çözebilirsin — `WHERE user_id` şartı, başkasının
cihazını koparıp onu kimliksiz kotaya düşürmeyi engeller.

Billing accrues to the widget owner's wallet (same path as phone calls).
Admission (mode/credit/daily-limit) is decided by _resolve_widget_voice.

Two guards run BEFORE admission, because admission burns the widget's
daily visitor quota on the way through:

  1. Origin allow-list. The chat endpoint has always enforced this; voice
     did not, so a widget could be embedded on any site and spend the
     owner's balance per minute. An Origin header is forgeable by a
     script, but it does stop the realistic case — someone dropping the
     public widget id into their own page.
  2. Per-IP daily cap. The per-widget cap alone lets one visitor exhaust
     the day's quota and lock out real ones; this bounds a single source.

post.description:
Create a new outbound calling campaign. The campaign is created in `draft` status; you typically follow up with:

1. `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/upload-csv` — bulk-add contacts from a CSV (or `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/contacts` to add them one by one).
2. `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/action` with `{action: "start"}` to begin dialing.

**Configuration**: `agent_id` (required), `from_number` (auto-assigned from agent's number if omitted), `max_concurrent` (parallel calls), `calls_per_minute` (rate limit), `retry_count` and `retry_delay_minutes` for failed attempts.

get.description: List all campaigns in the workspace, newest first. Filter by `status` (draft, running, paused, completed, cancelled) or by name via `search`. Use `limit`/`offset` for pagination.

200.description: Paginated list of campaigns with summary stats (contacts/completed/failed).

get.description: Retrieve a single campaign with progress stats: total contacts, called, completed, failed, in-progress. Use this to render a campaign detail dashboard or to drive a polling loop while the dialer is running.

200.description: Full campaign object including current status, totals and dialer counters.

patch.description: Update campaign settings. Most fields editable in any state except running agent_id.

post.summary: Control a campaign — start, pause, resume or cancel
post.description:
Drive the lifecycle of a campaign. Send `{action: "<verb>"}` where verb is one of:

- **start** — begin dialing (campaign moves draft → running)
- **pause** — temporarily halt the dialer (running → paused); in-flight calls are allowed to finish
- **resume** — pick up where it left off (paused → running)
- **cancel** — stop and finalize (any → cancelled); pending contacts will not be called

Common automation pattern: create campaign → upload CSV → start. Pause/resume is useful when integrating with business hours or external pacing logic.

200.description: Confirmation with the new campaign status.

400.description: Action not valid in current state (e.g. starting an already-running campaign).

get.description: List all contacts in a campaign. Each contact has a `status` (pending/calling/completed/failed/skipped) and, once dialed, a `call_id` you can use with `GET /v1/calls/{id}` to fetch the transcript. Filter by `status` to focus on failed contacts for follow-up or completed ones for reporting.

200.description: Paginated contacts with their per-contact dialer status and call results.

post.description: Add one or more contacts to a campaign by JSON payload. Each contact needs at minimum `phone_number`; `name` and a `variables` object (arbitrary key/value template variables consumed by the agent's system prompt) are optional. Duplicate phone numbers are silently skipped via `ON CONFLICT`. Only allowed while the campaign is in `draft` status — for bulk import prefer `POST /upload-csv`.

201.description: Number of contacts inserted (duplicates by phone are skipped).

400.description: Campaign is not in draft status.

delete.description: Remove all contacts from a campaign.

post.summary: Bulk-import contacts from a CSV file
post.description:
Bulk-import contacts into a campaign. Send a `multipart/form-data` request with a `file` field containing a CSV. Format:

- **Header row required**
- `phone` (or `phone_number`, `telefon`) — **required column**
- `name` (or `ad`, `isim`) — optional
- Any extra columns become per-contact template variables that the agent can interpolate into its system prompt or dialogue

**Limits**: max 5 MB, UTF-8 or Latin-1 encoded. Duplicate phone numbers within the same campaign are silently skipped. Allowed only while campaign status is `draft`.

201.description: Number of contacts inserted, skipped (duplicates) and any parse warnings.

400.description: Invalid CSV format, missing phone column, or campaign not in draft state.

Close call rows and web sessions that outlived their room.

Until now the only thing that closed a stranded row was somebody opening
the panel's call list, because the sweep lived inside that read path. A
call cut off mid-conversation — an agent restart, a browser that died
without reporting, a missed webhook — therefore showed as "in progress"
for as long as nobody looked, and for a browser room it did worse than
look wrong: `idx_web_sessions_one_open` allows a single open session per
interpreter, so one stranded row made that address unusable.

Everything here is time-guarded and idempotent, so running it every few
minutes is safe.

sending or recording anything.

Bekleme süresi dolan referans komisyonlarını ödenebilir yap.

Günlük cron. Komisyon `pending` doğuyor ve `referral_hold_days` (varsayılan
30 gün) sonra `payable` oluyor — bu süre iade penceresi: müşteri ödemesini
geri alırsa komisyon iptal ediliyor, ortaktan geri istenmiyor.

Send recurring 'come back' emails to verified-but-inactive users.

counts without sending or recording anything.

Run monthly recurring billing for phone numbers.

Intended to run daily via Cloud Scheduler. The logic is idempotent per day
(already-charged numbers skip). Handles the full lifecycle:

  1. Numbers where next_billing_at <= NOW() and status='active' without grace:
     - Try to deduct monthly_price_usd from wallet.
     - Success: advance next_billing_at +30d, log 'charged'.
     - Fail (insufficient balance): start 10-day grace, suspend_at=+3d,
       send warning email.

  2. Numbers in grace (grace_ends_at IS NOT NULL) not yet released:
     - Retry charge every day. Success → reactivate (clear grace, advance
       next_billing_at, send reactivation email).
     - If suspended_at passed and status='active': flip to 'suspended',
       send suspended email.

  3. Numbers where grace_ends_at <= NOW() and still unpaid:
     - Release at the carrier that holds it (Telnyx or Twilio), mark
       phone_numbers.status='inactive', send released email.

Scope: provider IN ('telnyx', 'twilio') — the carriers we rent from and
resell. `sip` and `netgsm` rows are deliberately out of scope: it is not
established that we carry a monthly cost for those, and several look like
customer-supplied trunks, where charging rent would be wrong.

Reconcile numbers stuck in provisioning limbo (> 10 min).

Two failure classes this handles:

  A. `phone_numbers.status = 'pending'` from /v1/numbers/purchase where the
     activation transaction never ran after Telnyx succeeded.
  B. `pending_number_purchases.status = 'ordering'` from the BUY_NUMBER
     webhook path where fulfill crashed after Telnyx order committed.

Strategy: ask Telnyx which numbers it thinks we own. If our 'pending'/'ordering'
number is in that list → activate it. If not → it was never ordered or was
released; clean up and (for purchase path) refund the user.

Run every 10 minutes via Cloud Scheduler.

Mark pending_number_purchases with expires_at < NOW() as 'expired'.

This frees the soft lock on the phone number so someone else can buy it.
Call via Cloud Scheduler every 5 minutes (TTL is 30 min so granularity is fine).

Agent'ın notification_targets kurallarını değerlendirip mesajları gönderir.

Best-effort: bir hedef patlarsa diğerleri ve çağrı akışı etkilenmez.

Ask Paddle what actually happened to checkouts we never heard back about.

Paddle only webhooks us on success. Every other ending — card declined,
dropped for fraud, 3-D Secure never completed, user closed the tab — is
silent, so our `payments` row stays 'pending' forever and all of those
endings look identical in the database.

On 24 Sep that blind spot hid the finding that mattered: of 59 stuck rows,
4 users had entered card details and been dropped with `fraud`. They were
not "users who didn't pay" — they were users we refused. Nothing in our
own data said so.

This walks recent stuck rows, asks Paddle for ground truth, and writes it
back so the funnel can be measured in SQL instead of by hand:

  - transaction completed  → mark 'completed' (webhook must have been missed)
  - a payment attempt was made and failed → 'failed' + the error code
  - still draft/ready with no attempt → leave 'pending', record last_checked

Deliberately does NOT credit wallets: crediting is the webhook's job and
doing it in two places is how double-credits happen. A completed-but-
uncredited row is surfaced as `needs_review` for a human instead.

Uzantı oturumlarının ölü kalanlarını kapat (cron, dakikada bir).

Heartbeat kesilip odada kalan bir istemci satırı `active` bırakır; kısmi
unique index yüzünden o cihaz bir daha oturum açamaz ve LiveKit odası
boşuna yaşar. Bu süpürge ikisini de toplar.

Havuz muhasebesi buna BAĞIMLI DEĞİL: `_pool_state` açık oturumlarda
duvar saatini kullandığı için cron hiç koşmasa da günlük tavan tutar —
bu projede "koruma yazılmış ama bağlanmamış" kalıbı birkaç kez gerçek
para kaybettirdi, o yüzden tek bacağa yaslanmıyoruz.

Attribution.title: Attribution
Attribution.description:
Where this user came from, captured in the browser on first touch.

GA4 loses the source when a visitor crosses from call2me.app to
dash.call2me.app, so every conversion landed in "Unassigned" and we
could not say how our first paying customer found us (14 Aug 2026).
This travels with the signup request instead, so attribution lives in
our own DB — independent of analytics and ad blockers.

Every field is optional: a direct visit legitimately has no referrer.
Lengths are capped because these strings come from the client.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Create and manage voice AI agents. An agent is the personality, voice and behavior of your AI — system prompt, model, language, voice, function-calling tools and (optionally) a knowledge base. You'll reference an `agent_id` from `/v1/calls`, `/v1/campaigns`, `/v1/schedules` and `/v1/widgets`.

tags.name: Calls
tags.description: Place outbound phone calls and inspect call history. `POST /v1/calls` starts an outbound call given an `agent_id`, a `from_number` and a `to_number`; the platform handles dialing, the AI conversation, recording and transcription. Use `GET /v1/calls/{id}` to retrieve the transcript, recording URL, status and post-call analysis.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: Run bulk outbound voice campaigns. Create a campaign with an agent and phone number, upload a CSV of contacts (`POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/upload-csv` — `phone` column required, `name` and any extra columns become per-contact variables), then start the dialer with `POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/action {action: "start"}`. Retry policy, concurrency and pacing are configurable.

tags.name: Schedules
tags.description: One-shot or recurring scheduled outbound calls. Use this for follow-ups, reminders, periodic check-ins. Recurrence supports daily/weekly/monthly cron-style rules.

tags.name: Phone Numbers
tags.description: Provision and assign phone numbers. Buy from supported regions, connect a SIP trunk for BYOC, or reserve a temporary demo number. Numbers can be assigned to a specific agent for inbound routing.

tags.name: Knowledge Base
tags.description: Upload documents (PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD) and URLs to give an agent domain-specific context. Vector search via pgvector + OpenAI embeddings; agents retrieve relevant chunks during conversation to answer factually. Reduces hallucination for product/policy/FAQ Q&A.

tags.name: Voices
tags.description: Browse available TTS voices from OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Cartesia and MiniMax. Filter by language, gender or provider; preview audio samples; reference a voice's `voice_id` when creating an agent.

tags.name: Widgets
tags.description: Embeddable chat/voice widgets you can drop into a website. Each widget is bound to an agent and produces a `<script>` snippet plus optional domain allow-list.

tags.name: Wallet
tags.description: Wallet balance, transaction history and top-ups. Calls, TTS and STT usage are billed per-minute against this balance.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description: Manage API keys used to authenticate against this API. Keys are workspace-scoped; rotate or revoke any time.

tags.name: WebSocket
tags.description: Real-time WebSocket connection for custom LLM integration.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: API health and status endpoints — useful for monitors and load balancers.
